status: Local freeze before new control generation, scoring and manuscript scoring; not external preregistration
question: Can repeated word-pair associations across separate physical folios distinguish a stable word code of coherent text from the specified copying mechanisms? Can non-message processes with persistent preferences also pass?
prior_exposure: All atlas views and former reserves are exposed. Published pair-replication results motivated this adaptation. Caesar/Dante sources were used before; Austen is newly acquired for this phase. No manuscript partition is historically blind.
method_status: Independent adaptation of Zhang and Sheng arXiv:2610.34499v1 section 5.1, not a reproduction of their unavailable implementation or 16-language experiment. Primary analysis retains all distinct pairs, avoiding a spelling-dependent mask under arbitrary word codes. Null expectations are exact combinatorial expectations rather than 20 sampled means.
input: ZL3b-n P0/P1 only, numeric folios, no @ or changing metadata; preserve uncertain tokens as unscored slots and drawing interruptions as segment boundaries. Only literal [a-z]+ words are scored; no word repair or uncertain-space choice. Keep segments with >=4 clean words, folios with >=40 clean words.
frame: Retain I/H/L strata with >=2 physical folios in each partition. Partition = floor(folio_number/5) mod 2, so adjacent pages of a folio stay together in five-folio blocks. Choose whole folios by SHA256(seed:folio), subject to <=24000 clean slots; recheck stratum support. Restore physical order. Frame selection inspects only metadata and token availability, never pair effects. All controls use exactly this ZL layout, holes, endpoints and partitions.
vocabulary: Top 300 word types by total frequency, ties by first occurrence, invariant under bijective word renaming. All unequal pairs; equal types are excluded. Vocabulary selection uses counts only and is invariant to within-page interior permutations.
counts: For each half, count segments containing both types at least once. Each unordered pair counts at most once per segment. Segment endpoints stay fixed; clear interior words are shuffled among clear interior slots on the SAME PAGE. Unknown slots stay fixed.
expected: Exact hypergeometric probability of presence of both types per segment, conditional on its fixed endpoints, number of clear interior slots and the page interior bag. Sum over segments. Thus page, section, attributed hand, quire, word frequencies, segment lengths and endpoints are preserved.
statistic: For each half, standardize pair residual (observed-expected)/sqrt(expected+0.5). Remove least-squares additive effects mu+a_i+a_j over the full off-diagonal symmetric pair matrix with sum(a)=0. Spearman correlation rho between the two halves over the upper triangle is the only primary statistic. No pair is selected by its observed effect.
null: 199 within-page interior permutations; recompute both count matrices, residuals and correlation for each. Exact expected matrix and count-selected vocabulary stay fixed. p=(1+number(null_rho>=observed_rho-1e-12))/200. Conditional exchangeability test, not causal or semantic proof. Serial dependence may violate the null.
detection: rho>=0.10 AND p<=0.01. Fixed before results; deliberately requires effect size as well as conditional significance. Not claimed a universal linguistic threshold.

controls.known: Two nonoverlapping stretches of frame token count from each of Caesar, Dante Inferno/Purgatorio and newly acquired Austen. Six base messages, each independently enciphered with a random bijective word code. Codebook is not passed to the scorer. These measure structural retention, not decryption accuracy.
controls.homophony: Four disjoint codewords per plaintext word, selected uniformly per occurrence, on the same six messages. Sensitivity only; a negative result does not reject homophonic ciphers.
controls.page_topic: No target plaintext. Opaque token frequencies from each base message; independent tokens with one of 16 arbitrary token-rank groups preferred per page, probability .8. Page topics should be removed by conditioning on page bags.
controls.local_copy: No target plaintext. Each page starts fresh. With probability .75 copy a uniformly selected token among the last 8 on the same page; otherwise sample the base unigram distribution. Equal-type pairs remain excluded.
controls.line_topic: No target plaintext. Same independent-token model as page_topic, but choose the arbitrary group per segment. Persistent line associations are a challenge to semantic specificity, not evidence of a hidden message.
controls.markov: No target plaintext. Generate from a first-order transition model of each base message: .8 empirical next-token distribution, .2 unigram fallback; restart each page. This inherits linguistic transition statistics without encoding a chosen passage. It is not claimed to have no accidental meaningful phrases.
controls.published_copy: Execute the unmodified TorstenTimm/SelfCitationTextgenerator at a6ede2202dd7ad6285ce2c007bf22c2a0e7709b7. Six fixed seeds 81..86, 6000 lines, default checked-in configuration except output location/name, seed and line count. Discard first 500 words, take exactly frame token count, reflow onto the common frame. Original generated lines and full effective configuration retained. Published seed vocabulary and glyph rules inherit Voynich observations; this is not a fresh manuscript-independent model.
controls.equal_budget: Same token count, layout, 300-type cap, partitions and 199 randomizations for each primary case. No parameter search or optimization. Six replicates per mechanism; generator replicates are not additional independent plaintext authors. Reflowed native generator geometry is explicitly a limitation.

gates.mechanical: Exact-expectation toy enumeration, independent count/residual arithmetic and bijective word-code invariance must pass.
gates.sensitivity: At least 5/6 bijective messages detected, at least 1/2 in EACH author, and at most 1/6 page_topic controls detected.
gates.copy_discrimination: Sensitivity gate plus at most 1/6 local_copy AND at most 1/6 published_copy detected. Only then may a manuscript result be interpreted as discriminating these tested copying settings from the tested stable word-code controls.
gates.semantic_specificity: Copy-discrimination gate plus at most 1/6 line_topic AND at most 1/6 markov detected. Passing would still cover only these generators, not establish meaning or decipherment.
gates.real_execution: If mechanical or sensitivity gate fails, do not score the manuscript. Otherwise score it once in ZL and IT, but freeze interpretation to the gates: if copy-discrimination fails, report structural association only and explicitly reject this test as a mechanism discriminator. Never infer translation.

fixed_sensitivities: Top-150 statistic on all six bijective controls and all six published-copy controls; if real execution is permitted, top 150 and comma-as-join transcription variant on ZL/IT using the same selected folios. All retained regardless of direction. No new significance claims or parameter tuning.
independence: New random streams and two Austen passages provide fresh control data after code freeze. Same-operator alternate arithmetic implementation is technical verification. Whole-folio partitions are internal validation. ZL/IT are sensitivity checks on one manuscript. Published generator code is an external implementation, not external confirmation of manuscript meaning. Human/linguistic independent confirmation remains absent.
preservation: Existing phases 1..23 and atlas remain unchanged. Failures, source versions, raw generated samples, mappings, null statistics and adaptations are saved. No publication, push or deployment.
